original_unit.text:
### Attack against negotiate: compensation

The negotiate player automatically loses; resolve the winner's ship destinations normally. The losing main player randomly takes one card from the opponent's hand for each of **their own ships actually lost to the warp**. Exclude allied losses: allies receive no compensation. If the opponent lacks sufficient cards, take the entire hand. Cards are taken without seeing their faces. For random hand-card selection, including compensation, you may see which card backs you select; “at random” means without seeing card faces (FAQ p5). Compensation is stolen hand cards; defender rewards are deck draws and/or warp retrieval.

No compensation for ships prevented from reaching the warp (Zombie/Observer) or removed by Void. Healer returning ships **after** they enter the warp does not remove compensation eligibility. Special winners such as Human/Pacifist can change who wins; compensation still requires the relevant attack-versus-negotiate condition.

original_unit.text:
### Flare system

Flares are not encounter cards. Each has printed Wild and Super effects, usage roles and timing. Normally use Wild; if it is your own alien's flare and your power is available, **you must use Super**, not choose Wild. If your power is lost or zapped, you can use only Wild until your power returns.

Return a flare to hand **immediately after its effect finishes**, rather than discard it, unless its effect states otherwise. A player may play **at most one flare per encounter**, and an individual flare can be used **only once per encounter even if it changes hands**. A Card Zap targeting the flare counts against the player's limit. Prevention of play differs from cancellation after play: see Anti-Matter's FAQ exception. If a Super enables a power use, that power can still be Cosmic Zapped even outside its usual role/phase. The flare remains in hand rather than being discarded or forced to Wild; Only Wild is available for an otherwise legal play while the power is zapped. Zapping the enabled power does not undo the already-played flare or permit a second play of it in the same encounter; the ordinary per-player and per-flare limits still apply. When your own Wild would otherwise be handed to your alien, keep it after resolution.

The FAQ quotes these Super effect timing clauses; they do not make a flare apply automatically in later encounters. Follow the full card for its other conditions and legal play.

| Original Super flare | Quoted effect timing |
|---|---|
| Kamikaze, Machine, Masochist | During each of **your own Regroup phases** |
| Miser | At the start of each of **your encounters** |
| Cudgel | Whenever you **use your power** |

These are effect timing clauses, not a reconstruction of an earlier permitted faceup-placement window (FAQ pp12,16–18).

### Power loss, zapping and timing

With fewer than **three home colonies**, immediately turn your alien sheet facedown and lose its power; you cannot use it one last time. Restore it faceup when you again occupy at least three home planets. Masochist expressly keeps its power with fewer colonies. Losing a power also removes that alien identity for power-dependent effects and access to its Super.

A power may be Cosmic Zapped **only when being used**, not preemptively. The bold-italic **use** on an alien sheet identifies its cancellable use. Cancel that effect and prevent further uses until the encounter ends, including when zapped during Start Turn. Clauses that do not require use—such as Warrior adding experience, Zombie liberating ships in a deal, or placing a Citadel—are not themselves zappable uses. Zapping a use does not disable such clauses.

You may wait to see a power's immediate effect (Chosen's drawn cards, Hate's selected discard, Philanthropist's offered card), but the zap window is short, in that same phase. You cannot wait until later reinforcements change the outcome and then undo an earlier power, or zap after moving to the next phase.

Effects associated with no player resolve last, after the player order. Resolve actual simultaneous contradictory effects in order: **offense; defense; other players clockwise starting left of offense**. First honor more specific before/after timing within a phase. Finish one effect before starting another, except a Zap or an effect expressly allowing interruption. An optional effect's owner may change their mind when another effect or timing order changes the game state. Alien powers are normally usable once per relevant context, unless their text says otherwise.

Cards may be legally played before compensation starts, but compensation does not permit arbitrary interruptions. Once an effect targets a hand and begins resolving, only a Zap or specific interrupt can intervene. You cannot wait for Hacker to select you and then dump reinforcements: the Reveal window has already passed.

original_unit.text:
### Flare system

Flares are not encounter cards. Each has printed Wild and Super effects, usage roles and timing. Normally use Wild; if it is your own alien's flare and your power is available, **you must use Super**, not choose Wild. If your power is lost or zapped, you can use only Wild until your power returns.

Return a flare to hand **immediately after its effect finishes**, rather than discard it, unless its effect states otherwise. A player may play **at most one flare per encounter**, and an individual flare can be used **only once per encounter even if it changes hands**. A Card Zap targeting the flare counts against the player's limit. Prevention of play differs from cancellation after play: see Anti-Matter's FAQ exception. If a Super enables a power use, that power can still be Cosmic Zapped even outside its usual role/phase. The flare remains in hand rather than being discarded or forced to Wild; Only Wild is available for an otherwise legal play while the power is zapped. Zapping the enabled power does not undo the already-played flare or permit a second play of it in the same encounter; the ordinary per-player and per-flare limits still apply. When your own Wild would otherwise be handed to your alien, keep it after resolution.

The FAQ quotes these Super effect timing clauses; they do not make a flare apply automatically in later encounters. Follow the full card for its other conditions and legal play.

| Original Super flare | Quoted effect timing |
|---|---|
| Kamikaze, Machine, Masochist | During each of **your own Regroup phases** |
| Miser | At the start of each of **your encounters** |
| Cudgel | Whenever you **use your power** |

These are effect timing clauses, not a reconstruction of an earlier permitted faceup-placement window (FAQ pp12,16–18).

### Flare system

Flares are not encounter cards. Each has printed Wild and Super effects, usage roles and timing. Normally use Wild; if it is your own alien's flare and your power is available, **you must use Super**, not choose Wild. If your power is lost or zapped, you can use only Wild until your power returns.

Return a flare to hand **immediately after its effect finishes**, rather than discard it, unless its effect states otherwise. A player may play **at most one flare per encounter**, and an individual flare can be used **only once per encounter even if it changes hands**. A Card Zap targeting the flare counts against the player's limit. Prevention of play differs from cancellation after play: see Anti-Matter's FAQ exception. If a Super enables a power use, that power can still be Cosmic Zapped even outside its usual role/phase. The flare remains in hand rather than being discarded or forced to Wild; Only Wild is available for an otherwise legal play while the power is zapped. Zapping the enabled power does not undo the already-played flare or permit a second play of it in the same encounter; the ordinary per-player and per-flare limits still apply. When your own Wild would otherwise be handed to your alien, keep it after resolution.

The FAQ quotes these Super effect timing clauses; they do not make a flare apply automatically in later encounters. Follow the full card for its other conditions and legal play.

| Original Super flare | Quoted effect timing |
|---|---|
| Kamikaze, Machine, Masochist | During each of **your own Regroup phases** |
| Miser | At the start of each of **your encounters** |
| Cudgel | Whenever you **use your power** |

These are effect timing clauses, not a reconstruction of an earlier permitted faceup-placement window (FAQ pp12,16–18).

### Power loss, zapping and timing

With fewer than **three home colonies**, immediately turn your alien sheet facedown and lose its power; you cannot use it one last time. Restore it faceup when you again occupy at least three home planets. Masochist expressly keeps its power with fewer colonies. Losing a power also removes that alien identity for power-dependent effects and access to its Super.

A power may be Cosmic Zapped **only when being used**, not preemptively. The bold-italic **use** on an alien sheet identifies its cancellable use. Cancel that effect and prevent further uses until the encounter ends, including when zapped during Start Turn. Clauses that do not require use—such as Warrior adding experience, Zombie liberating ships in a deal, or placing a Citadel—are not themselves zappable uses. Zapping a use does not disable such clauses.

You may wait to see a power's immediate effect (Chosen's drawn cards, Hate's selected discard, Philanthropist's offered card), but the zap window is short, in that same phase. You cannot wait until later reinforcements change the outcome and then undo an earlier power, or zap after moving to the next phase.

Effects associated with no player resolve last, after the player order. Resolve actual simultaneous contradictory effects in order: **offense; defense; other players clockwise starting left of offense**. First honor more specific before/after timing within a phase. Finish one effect before starting another, except a Zap or an effect expressly allowing interruption. An optional effect's owner may change their mind when another effect or timing order changes the game state. Alien powers are normally usable once per relevant context, unless their text says otherwise.

Cards may be legally played before compensation starts, but compensation does not permit arbitrary interruptions. Once an effect targets a hand and begins resolving, only a Zap or specific interrupt can intervene. You cannot wait for Hacker to select you and then dump reinforcements: the Reveal window has already passed.
